title: Servicing Policy Manual: Payment Posting on the Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Installment Sale Contract
content:
**Servicing Policy Manual — posting payments to a Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Installment Sale Contract.**

## Clauses in force

1. **Payable status.** A payment can be posted only while the contract status is active, repossession assigned, repossessed or deficiency. The status is read from the contract record before the payment is posted.
2. **Posting day.** A payment received before the product's payment cutoff time (Central Time) on a business day posts that day; a payment received later, or on a weekend or US federal holiday, posts the next business day.
3. Because interest is satisfied first and fees last, an installment paid in full within its grace period is never treated as late merely because an earlier fee remains unpaid.
4. **Principal-only payments.** A payment designated principal-only is accepted only when the contract shows 0 days past due and is applied to principal after accrued interest is satisfied; it never advances the next due date.
5. **Excess payments.** Payments in excess of the installment reduce principal and do not advance the next due date unless the customer pays a full additional installment.
6. **Channel fee.** The channel fee in the product's channel fee schedule is collected on top of the payment as a convenience fee and is never applied to the contract; the agent-assisted debit card fee is not charged when the payment is a reinstatement or redemption, which must be made in certified funds.
7. **Card limits.** Debit card payments are limited to the product's monthly card payment count per calendar month and to the product's maximum single card payment each.
8. **Certified funds.** While the contract's certified-funds-only date is on or after the posting date, only cashier's check, wire or MoneyGram payments are accepted.
9. When a payment carries a fee portion, that portion is booked as a fee payment against fees due; enrolling or unenrolling autopay is recorded on the contract.

## Retired clause

> "Each payment is applied in the allocation order: first to simple interest accrued over the interest accrual days at the contract APR on the product's day-basis year, then to principal until the installments due are satisfied, then to fees due, and any remainder to principal."

This clause is **no longer in force** as the handling basis for applying a payment; it has been superseded by the company's current posting basis for payments.

## Terms

- **Interest accrual days:** the calendar days, from the day after the date interest is paid to through the payment posting date, both inclusive, over which simple interest has accrued and is unpaid.
- **Installments due:** the past-due amount plus the monthly payment of the installment due on the next due date when that date falls within one month after the posting date — the amount a payment must reach before any part of it goes to fees.
- **Portions of a payment in the allocation order:** the interest portion is the lower of the payment and the accrued interest (principal balance times the contract APR divided by 100 and by the day basis, times the interest accrual days, rounded to the cent); the fee portion is the lower of the fees due and the part of the payment above the greater of the interest portion and the installments due, never below zero; the principal portion is the payment less the interest and fee portions.

## Certified-funds test, illustrated

*Hypothetical:* a contract's certified-funds-only date falls on a given day. A personal check posting on that same day is not accepted (the date is on or after the posting date); a personal check posting on the following day is accepted.

superseded_clauses: Each payment is applied in payment_allocation_order: first to simple interest accrued over retail_msr_interest_accrual_days at the contract apr on a per_diem_day_basis-day year, then to principal until retail_msr_installments_due is satisfied, then to fees due, and any remainder to principal.
